title: Kinematics
seo_title: Secondary 3 Physics: Kinematics Worksheets (O-Level 6091 with Answers)
standard_text: State what is meant by speed, velocity and acceleration; calculate average speed and acceleration = change in velocity ÷ time taken; plot and interpret distance-time and speed-time graphs, using the gradient to find speed or acceleration and the area under a speed-time graph to find distance; state that the acceleration of free fall near the Earth is constant at about 10 m/s²; describe the motion of objects falling with and without air resistance, including terminal velocity (summary of the Singapore-Cambridge O-Level Physics 6091 syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Secondary 3 O-Level Physics worksheets on kinematics: speed, velocity, acceleration, distance-time and speed-time graphs, free fall and terminal velocity. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Speed-time graph: gradient = acceleration, area = distance.
body_html:
How to think about it

Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity.

  • Average speed = total distance ÷ total time. Velocity is speed in a stated direction.
  • a = (v − u) ÷ t, in m/s². A negative value means slowing down (deceleration).
  • Distance-time graph: gradient = speed; flat line = at rest. Speed-time graph: gradient = acceleration; area = distance.
  • Without air resistance every object falls with g = 10 m/s². With air resistance a falling object reaches a terminal velocity.
Example

A bus goes from 4 m/s to 16 m/s in 6 s. Acceleration?

a = (16 − 4) ÷ 6

Answer: 2 m/s²

Example

A speed-time graph rises from 0 to 12 m/s in 4 s. Distance?

area of triangle = ½ × 4 × 12

Answer: 24 m

Example

A stone is dropped. Speed after 3 s? (g = 10 m/s²)

v = 0 + 10 × 3

Answer: 30 m/s

Common mistakes

  • Averaging the two speeds instead of dividing total distance by total time.
  • Reading a horizontal line on a distance-time graph as constant speed. It means the object is at rest.
  • Using the gradient of a speed-time graph for distance. Distance is the area under the graph.
  • Thinking heavier objects fall faster. Without air resistance all objects fall with the same acceleration.

faq.q: How do you find distance from a speed-time graph?
faq.a: Work out the area under the graph: triangles (½ × base × height) and rectangles (base × height), then add them.
The constant speed a falling object reaches when air resistance has grown to equal its weight, so the resultant force is zero.

faq.q: What value of g is used in O-Level Physics?
faq.a: The acceleration of free fall near the Earth is taken as 10 m/s² (the gravitational field strength is 10 N/kg).

items.e: a = (0 − 9) ÷ 2 = −4.5 m/s². The minus sign means it is slowing down (deceleration).

items.q: What is the difference between speed and velocity?
